It goes like this: a guitarist with a four-decade career, a signature Ibanez, a wall of Marshalls and access to literally any overdrive ever built gets asked which pedal matters most to him. He names one that costs less than a set of strings and a decent lunch. GG-ARTICLE-AFTER-INTRO That is the TC Electronic MojoMojo Overdrive, and the guitarist is Paul Gilbert. Speaking to Guitarist magazine in 2016 — an ordinary interview, not a promo video, not a launch campaign — Gilbert was asked about pedals and gave one of the more honest answers in the genre. He described his ideal pedal as a “placebo box” that does nothing but makes you feel like you’re playing better. Then he named the actual one. “As far as specific pedals, the one that’s really been a mainstay is the TC Electronic MojoMojo,” he said. “It’s really a normal [overdrive] pedal. There’s nothing unusual about it except it just sounds good.” Nothing unusual about it except it just sounds good. If you had to compress the entire appeal of this pedal into ten words, that would be the ten. And it is the reason the MojoMojo, fifteen years after launch, is still in production, still in the top few hundred distortion pedals at Europe’s largest music retailer, and still selling for less than fifty dollars — a price that has caused more confusion about its quality than any review ever could. This is the story of a genuinely great cheap overdrive, the enormous artist roster attached to it (most of which does not survive scrutiny), and the one name on that roster that survives beautifully. How to Get the Tone ↓ Where the MojoMojo Came From: The Noise People Get Into Dirt TC Electronic was founded in 1976 in Denmark by brothers Kim and John Rishøj. As Premier Guitar ‘s Matthew Holliman put it in the pedal’s launch review, they were self-described “experts on noise” who set out to clean up a guitar world full of crackling, popping effects. Their breakthrough was the SCF Stereo Chorus Flanger, which won over guitarists and keyboard players largely because it was quiet — a competitive advantage that sounds trivially boring today and was anything but in 1980. sources.excerpt: TC Electronic MojoMojo Overdrive – Pedal Wiki Pedal Wiki Guitar effect pedal database TC Electronic MojoMojo Overdrive MojoMojo is an analog overdrive pedal by TC Electronic. It is designed to sound like an amp, to preserve dynamic of the original playing and maintain clarity even in complex chords. MojoMojo features four knobs and one switch Drive knob (controls gain) Level (output stage attenuator) Bass (High-pass EQ) Treble Internally, MojoMojo circuit is nearly the same as the Dark Matter with slight changes: Voice input does not alter frequency response but only changes pre-gain signal level (analog of turning down the volume knob on guitar). Wider tone control Lower pre-gain signal boost Higher gain range Higher post-gain boost Source: Traced schematic of MojoMojo by DraftYeti5608 on Reddit. Sound demo by TC Electronic The list of artists endorsing MojoMojo includes Tom Hamilton of Aerosmith and Scott Ian of Anthrax. Paul Gilbert is also a known user of the pedal and even has his signature edition released by TC Electronic in 2021: Type: Overdrive Analog True bypass Inputs: 1 x 6.25mm (1 x 1/4″) TS Outputs: 1 x 6.25mm (1 x 1/4″) TS Dimensions: 72 x 122 x 50 mm Power consumption: 9V Polarity: center-negative In production since: April 2011 Analogs: Ibanez TS9 TubeScreamer , Boss OD-1X OverDrive Page on the manufacturer’s site Shops: Thomann , Reverb
